name: Batch
comments:
Array members and an anonymous class that uses its own members.

Both were blind spots found by auditing a real corpus (commons-lang), not by this corpus: arrays were present but nothing ever read `array.length`, and an anonymous class was present but nothing inside it touched its own fields.

`counts.length` and `int[]::new` declare their member on the ARRAY type. An array is not an entity, and its component type does not own those members — attributing them to the component invented a stub class named `int` and an access on `com.acme.order.Money` that the source never writes.

The anonymous `Priceable` is identified by `#file:line`; Spoon names it `Batch$1`, so any edge that names it from a type REFERENCE must be translated back, or one declared class ends up with two ids and the second is laundered into a stub carrying the corpus's own package.

name: OrderService

Billing and archival. Both {@code archive} overloads take a parameter whose
simple name is {@code List}; only their packages differ.

name: StockGuard
comments:
Throw-site regression case: a guard clause and a rethrow must each emit a
{@code throws} edge anchored at its own statement, and the {@code throws}
clause on {@code check} must stay a plain reference (propagation, not a
failure exit).
